title: "I will not rise"
hook: he resolves not to move until he awakens

segments.voice: Yesterday, assattha, the fig tree: a grass-cutter's gift spread as a seat facing east. A seat is a decision.

A workout you'll quit if it gets too hard. A writing session with the phone face-up beside you. Ten minutes of meditation, and at minute four a voice says, you know, that's probably enough. An exit built into everything can feel safe. It also means never finding out what's on the other side of staying. The wanderer is sitting on his seat of grass under the great fig tree, facing east. The sun is going down. And before the night begins, he makes a vow.
screen: `AN EXIT BUILT INTO EVERYTHING.` → `AT MINUTE FOUR...` → `A VOW AT SUNSET.`

segments.voice: The later telling gives the vow in dramatic words. Let my skin and sinews and bones dry up. Let the flesh and blood in my body wither. But I will not rise from this seat until I have found complete awakening. It sounds like the old austerities, but it isn't. He's not starving now; he's eaten. He's not forcing his breath. He's just decided not to leave. That difference, forcing or staying, is the whole lesson of the last two weeks. The Pali canon has a similar resolve in the Buddha's own words: let only skin and sinews and bones remain, but my effort will not slacken until I reach what can be reached. And what he's staying for has a name: bodhi. It means awakening, from a root, budh, that means to wake up, to become aware, to understand. The same root is in the word Buddha, which comes soon. In Buddhist teaching, bodhi is not a trance, or a vision, or a feeling of bliss. It's pictured as waking up, the way you wake from a dream and see the room as it actually is. That's why the tree became the Bodhi tree, and the place Bodh Gaya. Staying put, in Buddhist practice, doesn't mean gritting your teeth through pain. It means not running. When restlessness says get up, you notice it, and stay. When boredom says check your phone, you notice it, and stay. The noticing is the practice.
screen: `I WILL NOT RISE FROM THIS SEAT.` · `NOT FORCING. STAYING.` · `BODHI — FROM BUDH, TO WAKE UP.` · `STAYING PUT IS NOT RUNNING.` · then, large: `STAY PUT.`

segments.voice: Make a small vow, the size of today: for these two minutes, I'll stay, not perfectly still, not perfectly calm, just here. When the mind says that's enough, notice it and stay; when an itch comes, see if it passes; when a thought pulls you away, come back to the breath. You're not fighting anything, just not leaving.
Bodhi. Awakening, from the root budh, to wake up. What the wanderer vowed not to rise without, and the name of the tree he sat beneath.
Your line: stay put. The night under the tree is just beginning. See you there tomorrow.

howItsDone: Some Buddhist meditators begin a sit or a retreat by making a quiet resolve (adhitthana) to stay for a set time, and resolve is counted among the perfections in Theravada teaching.

Yes. He planned to starve himself until awakening came.
